ogTitle: 10 Most Popular Restaurants in Chiang Rai 2026 — Eat Like the Locals
ogDesc: Riverside cafés on the Kok, a hilltop tea plantation, a legendary nam ngiao shop, khao soi, and Northern Thai kantoke — 10 top Chiang Rai restaurants with signature dishes and prices.
eyebrow: Eat like the locals in Chiang Rai · Updated 2026
intro: Chiang Rai is a city where good food runs from morning to late at night — hot rice noodles with nam ngiao in the late morning, a riverside café on the Kok in the afternoon, and Northern Thai kantoke by evening. We've gathered the 10 restaurants that locals and visitors mention most, all in one place. There's a beautiful-view café, a legendary nam ngiao shop, and bold Northern Thai cooking. Choose by meal and budget.

blocks.html:
If you think about Chiang Rai from a food angle, the charm is that genuinely authentic Northern Thai food is still easy to find in everyday life — not just on tourist menus. In the late morning, people here queue for rice noodles with nam ngiao and khao kan jin in the San Khok Noi area; in the afternoon they drive up the hill to sip tea at the plantation, or sit by the Kok River at one of the pretty cafés. Come evening they gather around a spread of khua laab, gaeng hang le, and Northern Thai dishes in kantoke style in town. Northern food in Chiang Rai runs smooth and aromatic with clear spicing, not heavy on sweetness — eat it with sticky rice and you lose track of time.

This list covers restaurants that are genuinely well-known and verified. From Chivit Thamma Da Coffee House — the European-colonial riverside café that's become a landmark for café lovers — to Choui Fong Tea Cafe, the Mae Chan hillside landmark famous for its green tea cake, Pa Suk Nam Ngiao, one of the city's oldest nam ngiao shops, Paam Sai Ua, which puts a fun spin on Northern food, and Toke-Tong and Salungkham, which serve kantoke with traditional performances. Every restaurant on this list is currently open, has a clear signature dish, and once you finish reading you can decide exactly which meal to have where. Save some appetite — Chiang Rai has more good food than most people expect.

blocks.name: Chivit Thamma Da Coffee House, Bistro & Bar
blocks.area: Mueang Chiang Rai District, Chiang Rai
blocks.signature: Pineapple fried rice, Truffle Cheese Burger, homemade banoffee and fresh-baked cakes
blocks.descHtml:
If there's one restaurant in Chiang Rai that people never stop talking about, it has to be Chivit Thamma Da Coffee House, Bistro & Bar. A family-run spot on the Kok River at Ban Rong Suea Ten, Soi 3, Rim Kok subdistrict — café, bistro, and bar all in one. The building is decorated in old European colonial style: wooden ceilings, vintage furniture, a lawn and shaded garden stretching down to the river. That kind of atmosphere suits anyone who wants to sit slowly, sip coffee, eat sweets, or celebrate a special meal with someone important.

The menu items people order most are the pineapple fried rice — great to look at and smooth in flavor — the Truffle Cheese Burger with its firm patty and warm truffle aroma, and the homemade desserts that are genuinely the kitchen's pride: banoffee and fresh-baked cake especially. The bakery here produces its own bread every day — sourdough, scones, cakes, and pies. Most reviews praise the desserts as outstanding, the coffee as easy to drink, and the Thai-Western food as carefully executed. Many people say they make a point of coming here every visit to Chiang Rai.

Prices are mid-range — around 251–500 THB per person. Desserts start at around 128 THB for the banoffee, which is fair for the atmosphere and quality. Open every day 09:00–22:00. Come for a riverside breakfast, a quiet afternoon tea in the garden, or a candlelit dinner on the second-floor balcony. Google rating sits at 4.6 from thousands of reviews, reflecting sustained and genuine popularity.

Good to know: during weekends and evenings it gets very busy. If you want a river-view table or a spot on the upper balcony, call ahead to book, and allow plenty of time — this is a slow-life restaurant, not a quick stop. Groups can use the spacious grounds; couples will find it romantic. A perfectly calibrated first meal or special occasion when you arrive in Chiang Rai.
blocks.bestFor: Special riverside meal, couples, café lovers

blocks.name: Choui Fong Tea Cafe
blocks.area: Pa Sang, Mae Chan District, Chiang Rai
blocks.signature: Green tea cake, honey-lemon tea, drinks made from the plantation's own tea leaves
blocks.descHtml:
When it comes to a café you absolutely must visit in Chiang Rai, Choui Fong Tea Cafe is one of the first names everyone thinks of. This is a large tea plantation in the hills of Mae Chan District, growing tea for over 40 years and now run as a café in the middle of the plantation where you can sip tea, eat pastries, and look out over layer after layer of green mountains. It's perfect for café lovers, photography enthusiasts, people wanting to escape the heat up the hill, or families looking for a relaxed outing. The open space, cool breeze, and genuinely good views are exactly as advertised.

The menu item people talk about most is the green tea cake — soft crumb, just the right intensity of tea flavor without being cloyingly sweet — along with the green tea blend and drinks made from the plantation's own leaves. Another popular order is the honey-lemon tea, refreshing alongside the views. The green tea roll has also drawn praise for its natural flavor. True tea lovers consistently say the tea here is fragrant and high quality, which is what Choui Fong does best.

Pricing is standard café level, around 101–250 THB per person, with drinks starting around 70 THB. An honest observation from real reviews: most people come for the views and the drinks and pastries rather than a full meal. Some note that souvenir products in the shop are on the expensive side, and on weekends it gets very crowded — parking and seating may involve a wait. Coming in the morning is more comfortable.

Open daily 08:30–17:30. The plantation sits on a hill some distance from Chiang Rai town — the road up has a few bends but is perfectly driveable. With tiered tea-field views and drinks made from leaves grown right here, Choui Fong has become a landmark that almost everyone visiting Chiang Rai wants to stop at.
blocks.bestFor: Café lovers, tea plantation photography, family outings

blocks.name: Pa Suk Nam Ngiao
blocks.area: Mueang Chiang Rai District, Chiang Rai
blocks.signature: Rice noodles with nam ngiao (pork and beef), khao kan jin
blocks.descHtml:
If you want authentic, original nam ngiao in Chiang Rai, Pa Suk Nam Ngiao in Soi San Khok Noi 5 is the name locals mention first. The restaurant has been open for over 50 years — a small shophouse without many seats, unpretentious and honest. It suits anyone who wants genuinely local food rather than a prettily decorated restaurant. The signature order is rice noodles with nam ngiao, available with pork or beef, and if you prefer a noodle-style bowl there's kuay tiao nam ngiao too. Khao kan jin and rice noodles in nam ya are available for variety.

What makes this place special is the deeply concentrated nam ngiao broth — fragrant with the spice paste, with cotton-flower petals, tomatoes, and pork blood all present in the true Northern style. Ground pork is used instead of pork bones, making it easier to eat. Reviews consistently say the flavor is rounded, medium-hot, not too salty, and generous in portion for the price. Those who prefer less heat can add chilies themselves. Khao kan jin and kaep moo are popular side orders that pair perfectly. That kind of flavor is exactly what makes people keep coming back.

Very affordable — rice noodles with nam ngiao start at around 40 THB, 50 THB for the special, and 60 THB for the large. Located in town, you can drive into Soi San Khok Noi 5 without difficulty, though parking is limited and several reviewers note it can be a challenge. Open Tuesday–Sunday, 09:30–14:30. Closed on Mondays. Google rating 4.4 stars from over a thousand reviews, reflecting genuine and sustained love for this place.

Worth knowing: the restaurant is very popular, and from mid-morning to noon the queue is long for both eating in and takeaway. Some days items sell out before closing time. If you're planning a visit, arriving a little earlier gives you the best chance of a complete menu. Cash only, no Wi-Fi — come prepared and you won't miss this bowl.
blocks.bestFor: Morning to midday — authentic nam ngiao

blocks.name: Melt in Your Mouth
blocks.area: Kok Riverside, Rob Wiang, Mueang Chiang Rai District, Chiang Rai
blocks.signature: Blueberry pancakes, strawberry waffle, thin-crust pizza, Japanese cheesecake
blocks.descHtml:
If you want a pretty riverside café in Chiang Rai for a long, relaxed sit, Melt in Your Mouth has been a well-known name since the 2010s. The restaurant is a large English-cottage-style house in a green garden beside the Kok River in the Koh Loi area, Rob Wiang. A tree-lined walkway leads inside, where the décor runs cream tones with vintage furniture. There's both an air-conditioned interior section and an outdoor riverside section with a cool breeze. It suits anyone who wants to eat sweets, sip coffee, take photos, or bring family and friends for a relaxed meal.

The most-ordered signature items are the blueberry pancakes — fluffy with a good blueberry sauce — strawberry waffles, thin-crust pizza that multiple reviewers praise for the cheese, and Japanese cheesecake with a light, airy texture. Beyond desserts there's gelato, milkshakes, and savory items like khao soi with beef, pasta, and steak. The coffee uses beans from Doi Chang and Doi Pangkhon, both respected Chiang Rai coffee origins.

Real-review sentiment is fairly consistent: the riverside atmosphere and views are the primary selling point, especially in the evenings. Desserts and drinks are well executed. Staff are friendly. A portion of reviews note that savory dishes can be inconsistent, and some dishes come slowly or feel expensive for the portion size. If you're coming mainly to sit and enjoy desserts with coffee, this hits the mark.

Around 250–500 THB per person for a full order; coming for light desserts and drinks runs about 100–250 THB. Open daily, approximately 09:00–20:00. On weekends it gets busy — booking ahead is worthwhile. Located near Koh Loi Park, a short drive from the town center.
blocks.bestFor: Riverside café lovers — a long afternoon of coffee, desserts, and photos

blocks.name: Paam Sai Ua
blocks.area: Mueang Chiang Rai District, Chiang Rai
blocks.signature: Sai ua cheese balls, sai ua nam phrik num pizza, krapao sai ua moo narak, Beethoven coffee
blocks.descHtml:
If you want Northern Thai food in Chiang Rai with a creative twist — not the standard kantoke format — Paam Sai Ua is the restaurant many friends love to take guests to. The name "Paam" is a Northern Thai word meaning a shelter where people gather. The restaurant is on San Kok Chang Road near the town center, designed in contemporary Lanna style with high open ceilings, traditional decorative elements, multiple zones including a café area, a main dining hall, and an outdoor garden. It can seat hundreds of people and works well for families, groups of friends, or couples wanting a relaxed and photogenic atmosphere.

The star is sai ua (Northern Thai herb sausage) — and the kitchen has a lot of fun with it. The most-ordered items are sai ua cheese balls, fried hot with the cheese stretching inside; sai ua nam phrik num pizza, putting Northern Thai flavors on a pizza base in a way that actually works; and krapao sai ua moo narak, a fiercely seasoned stir-fry with rich, full-mouthful flavor. If you're in a group, the Lanna Paam set is recommended — served on a multi-compartment tray with nam phrik ong, sai ua, gaeng hang le, and kaep moo so you can sample everything in one sitting. Health-conscious diners can also order keto sai ua with no MSG and no added sugar.

Another must-try is the Beethoven coffee — espresso mixed with chilies and wild honey, delivering coffee flavor, honey sweetness, then a subtle kick of heat. Unusual and very much talked-about. Most reviews praise the generous portions, the flavor profile that feels traditional but looks modern, and friendly staff who speak some English. Prices are accessible, mostly 100–250 THB, with some specialties running higher.

A small note: the outdoor garden section can have mosquitoes in the evening despite the restaurant's pest control efforts. Choosing an indoor seat avoids this. Parking is easy. Open daily from morning through the evening — breakfast, lunch, and dinner all work. This is a restaurant that makes Northern food approachable without abandoning the original flavors, which is why both locals and visitors keep talking about it.
mustOrder: Sai ua nam phrik num pizza
blocks.bestFor: Family or group meal — Northern Thai food with a modern spin in a great atmosphere
blocks.spice: Medium heat (some dishes bold, e.g. krapao sai ua moo narak)

blocks.name: Laab Sanam Kila
blocks.area: Mueang Chiang Rai District, Chiang Rai
blocks.signature: Khua laab moo, jin som mok, fried chicken with makwaen, pak kat jo
blocks.descHtml:
Ask someone in Chiang Rai where to get bold, home-style Northern Thai food and Laab Sanam Kila usually comes up near the top of the list. Located in a soi off the front of the provincial stadium, Rob Wiang subdistrict, the restaurant has been open long enough to become a fixture in many families' memories — a local restaurant where Chiang Rai residents bring guests from out of town. The decor is simple Lanna style, plenty of tables, comfortable seating. It's ideal for groups who want to order many dishes to share.

The dish everyone orders is the khua laab moo — genuinely Northern in flavor, fragrant with the laab spice mix, properly dry-fried for a clear, concentrated aroma, eaten with hot sticky rice. Another frequently praised dish is jin som mok, mentioned for its generous portion and rounded sour flavor. The fried chicken with makwaen comes out fragrant with the distinctive pepper, topped with crispy fried makwaen leaves. Pak kat jo with blood is rich and deeply flavored in the full Northern style. Anyone who loves bold Northern flavors should be satisfied. There's also fried snapper with garlic and nam phrik kha served with steamed meat that many people keep coming back for.

Prices are easy on the wallet — around 101–250 THB per person, so ordering multiple dishes for the table stays affordable. The restaurant was refurbished and looks cleaner now. Parking is available beside the stadium. Open approximately 10:00–20:00 daily, works for both lunch and dinner. Review ratings on food sites run around 3.8–4.0 stars with consistent foot traffic.

A small note: some reviews mention that after expansion the flavor of a few dishes shifted slightly from the original, and on busy days the wait can be longer. Arriving before peak meal hours is more comfortable. Overall, for classic Northern Thai food with genuine flavor, this is a restaurant worth the trip.
blocks.bestFor: Group outing — bold, authentic Northern Thai food

blocks.name: Salungkham
blocks.area: Mueang Chiang Rai District, Chiang Rai
blocks.signature: Grilled sai ua, gaeng hang le, nam phrik num, khua laab, mixed grill / kantoke set
blocks.descHtml:
If you want genuinely original Northern Thai food in Chiang Rai — not a tourist-adapted version — Salungkham is usually the first name locals think of. The restaurant has been part of the city for decades, on Phahonyothin Road in the town center. The building is a Lanna-style wooden house with a serious, warm-toned interior decor section and a shaded outdoor garden. It's ideal for families or groups who want to order multiple dishes and share them together.

The dishes people order most and can't miss are grilled sai ua — fragrant with the curry-paste aroma, firm and not greasy — and gaeng hang le, simmered until the pork is soft and yielding with a beautifully balanced sweet-salty flavor. For nam phrik lovers, ordering both nam phrik num and nam phrik e-kae alongside blanched vegetables and kaep moo is the right move. Groups wanting to eat kantoke-style can order mixed grill, pork neck, pork ribs, and smoked pork to share. Khua laab is another frequently praised dish.

On flavor, most reviews are positive — genuinely authentic Northern Thai taste, fair prices for a comfortable sit-down restaurant, good service, and generous portions. Most dishes are 100–250 THB, averaging 250–500 THB per person for a group spread. A few things to note: at busy times there can be a wait, some menu items may be unavailable, and the outdoor garden section can have mosquitoes in the evening — bring repellent for peace of mind.

Open daily approximately 10:30–22:00. Plenty of parking. Seating for well over a hundred guests. English-speaking staff are limited, so foreign visitors may need to point at the menu or use photos. Overall, if you want serious Northern food in a Lanna atmosphere without having to dress up, Salungkham is the right balance of flavor, price, and setting.
mustOrder: Nam phrik num + nam phrik e-kae
blocks.bestFor: Family or group dinner — serious about Northern Thai food

blocks.name: Khao Soi Islam Chiang Rai
blocks.area: Mueang Chiang Rai District, Chiang Rai
blocks.signature: Khao soi kai, khao soi neua, khao mok kai
blocks.descHtml:
If you want genuine Haw Chinese Muslim-style khao soi in Chiang Rai, the restaurant in the soi near Samakkhi Wittayakhom School in the town center is the place to visit. The restaurant has been open for multiple generations — many people call it the "ninety-year khao soi" — a small shop with a deliberately short menu: just khao soi, khao mok, and khao luang kai. But everything is made with care. It suits anyone who wants a consistent original flavor, whether locals, nearby students, or travelers tracking down old-school restaurants.

The must-order items are khao soi kai and khao soi neua. The broth is a clear style, gently fragrant with curry paste and coconut milk — not thick or cloying the way many khao soi restaurants make it. Smooth, tender noodles. The standout item that reviews consistently single out is the restaurant's house pickled vegetables — intensely sour and tangy, cutting through richness beautifully, and many people ask for extra servings. Khao mok kai is another dish not to miss — aromatic with spices, chicken marinated until it's tender throughout, excellent alongside the hot broth. Anyone who wants crunch can add fried chicken skin as a small extra.

Very affordable — khao soi is around 40 THB per bowl, and khao mok kai is similarly in the double digits. A filling meal that doesn't require any second thought. The restaurant is a classic old shophouse from the 1990s with a visible noodle-blanching counter — authentically community-restaurant in style. Located in the town center near B2 Hotel. Open daily from 07:00–16:00 — breakfast or lunch.

This restaurant has stayed in Chiang Rai people's hearts for so long because the recipe has been kept steady for years. It's halal food, suitable for everyone. Worth knowing: the restaurant is small, parking is limited, and some items sell out in the afternoon. If you're planning a visit, aim to come in the mid-morning for a complete menu. Once you've eaten here, you'll understand why this place has lasted as long as it has.
blocks.bestFor: Morning to midday — tracing old-school restaurants

blocks.name: Toke-Tong
blocks.area: Mueang Chiang Rai District, Chiang Rai
blocks.signature: Kantoke set, khao soi with chicken drumstick, rich gaeng hang le
blocks.descHtml:
If you want a full Northern Thai kantoke dinner in a genuinely Lanna atmosphere in Chiang Rai, Toke-Tong is the restaurant many people think of first. The space is a large old wooden house in the Mueang District, with a kantoke courtyard at the back decorated with yi-peng lanterns. Every evening there's traditional dance and khum mueang music alongside the meal. It suits families and friend groups who want a long, leisurely dinner with a performance — not a quick à la carte stop, but a meal where you settle in and absorb the Northern atmosphere.

The dishes to order are the kantoke set, which brings a full spread of Northern dishes in one sitting — nam phrik num, kaep moo, sai ua, gaeng hang le, and blanched vegetables — so you get a complete taste in one order. Smaller groups can order dishes individually. The items that come up most in reviews are the khao soi with chicken drumstick, with a fragrant, herbal broth and tender meat, and the rich gaeng hang le with its well-rounded sweet-salty depth and meltingly soft pork. Side items like fried chicken wings, khua laab, and tom yam fish are also well-regarded.

An honest observation: Google scores around 4.3 from several hundred reviews — solid and consistent. Some reviews note that a few dishes lean a little sweet, adjusted for tourist palates, and service can slow during peak periods. Prices are higher than a street-side khao soi stall, averaging 100–300 THB per dish, but for the wooden house setting, kantoke, and live performance it's fair for a special meal.

Location and hours: on the old Phahonyothin Road in Rob Wiang, Mueang Chiang Rai — easy to reach from the town center. Open daily from around midday through late night. The best atmosphere is the evening meal with the performance. In-house parking is limited but roadside parking is available. If you're visiting during high season or with a large group, calling ahead to book the kantoke courtyard is the safer move. The reason this restaurant stays popular is that it delivers Northern Thai food, Lanna atmosphere, and traditional performance in one place — for a special dinner, it delivers.
blocks.bestFor: Full Northern Thai kantoke dinner — family or group, with traditional performance atmosphere

blocks.name: Hlu Lam Rob Wiang
blocks.area: Mueang Chiang Rai District, Chiang Rai
blocks.signature: Khua laab moo, gaeng ho, sai ua, Northern Thai appetizer platter, stir-fried pakud fern
blocks.descHtml:
Hlu Lam Rob Wiang is a long-established Northern Thai restaurant on the Kok River that both locals and visitors have been naming as their go-to for Northern food for decades. If a friend asks where to eat Northern Thai food for the first time in Chiang Rai, this is the answer you can give with confidence — it combines genuine Northern flavors, a comfortable riverside setting, and adequate parking in one place. It works well for families or groups. The restaurant has both an air-conditioned section upstairs and floating raft seating beside the river with a cool breeze all day. The walls are covered with photographs accumulated over decades, telling the restaurant's own story.

The menu item that consistently gets the most mentions is the khua laab moo — minced pork dry-fried with herb spices until fragrant, deeply flavored with every bite, usually served alongside crispy fried intestines for contrast. One review goes as far as calling it "the best" in the restaurant. For groups, the Northern Thai appetizer platter is recommended — great value, delivering sai ua, kaep moo, moo yo, nam phrik num, and accompanying vegetables in one plate. Other frequently ordered dishes include gaeng ho, gaeng hang le, jo pak kat with pork ribs, stir-fried pakud fern, and fried naem with pork ribs. The flavor is authentically Northern, not sweetened for tourists.

Prices are accessible — most dishes run 79–299 THB, averaging about 100–250 THB per person, fair for the portions served. Located on Khwaewai Road, Rob Wiang subdistrict, Mueang Chiang Rai. Open daily approximately 10:30–20:00. The riverside view at sunset is particularly good in the evening. Worth knowing: the restaurant closes fairly early, and during busy periods food can come slowly — allow extra time, and if you're coming as a large group, calling ahead for a table is worth it. When you're in Chiang Rai and want Northern food with a proper atmosphere, this is the reliable choice.
blocks.bestFor: First meal in Chiang Rai — family or group

blocks.title: What to know before you eat in Chiang Rai

items.title: Getting around
items.text: Grab is available in the town center but fewer cars than Bangkok or Chiang Mai. Many popular restaurants are in the Rob Wiang area and walkable from each other. Choui Fong Tea Cafe is on Doi Mae Chan, around 40 km from town — rent a car or book a driver.

items.title: Payment
items.text: Street food stalls, nam ngiao shops, and khao soi restaurants mostly take cash. Carry smaller bills. Cafés and sit-down restaurants in town often accept PromptPay transfers and some take cards.

items.title: Beat the queues
items.text: Nam ngiao and khao soi are late-morning-to-afternoon shops — going before 11am means a complete menu and no long wait. Popular cafés and kantoke restaurants on weekends get very busy; going earlier or booking in advance helps.

items.title: Language and menus
items.text: Tourist-facing cafés and restaurants like Chivit Thamma Da, Choui Fong, and kantoke restaurants usually have English menus. Street food may be Thai only — pointing or using the Thai name for popular dishes like khao soi or nam ngiao works fine.

items.title: Flavors and heat
items.text: Northern Thai food is rounded and medium-heat overall, but khua laab and some nam phrik dishes are genuinely spicy. If you can't take much chili, ask the kitchen for less spice. Northern dishes are typically eaten with sticky rice.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: Tipping is not required at Thai restaurants. Street food stalls don't expect tips. At sit-down restaurants and cafés with good service, leaving small change or rounding up is a gesture that staff appreciate — but it's not a required custom.

blocks.title: Planning your eating in Chiang Rai in one day
blocks.html:
Try this sequence for a full day of good eating. Start late morning with rice noodles with nam ngiao at Pa Suk Nam Ngiao in the San Khok Noi area, or khao soi kai at Khao Soi Islam Chiang Rai — both are midday restaurants that typically close in the afternoon, so going too late risks missing out.

In the afternoon, move into café mode. If you have a car, drive up to Choui Fong Tea Cafe in Mae Chan to sip tea with green tea cake and take in the plantation views. If you'd rather stay in town, Chivit Thamma Da or Melt in Your Mouth on the Kok River both work well. In the evening, gather for Northern food at Paam Sai Ua for a creative take on the classics, or head to Toke-Tong or Salungkham if you want kantoke atmosphere with traditional performance.

blocks.text: If you're eating across multiple meals in Chiang Rai, staying in the town center for a night or two is the most convenient base — most of the top restaurants are in the Rob Wiang and Kok Riverside area. Book a well-located stay ahead of time so you can eat at your own pace.

faq.q: Which restaurant is the most famous in Chiang Rai?
faq.a: Measured by popularity and review scores, Chivit Thamma Da Coffee House ranks at the top for café lovers (around 4.6 stars from thousands of reviews). For Northern Thai food, Choui Fong Tea Cafe on Doi Mae Chan is the hilltop landmark most associated with Chiang Rai — famous for green tea cake and plantation views. Both are widely known to Thai and international visitors alike.

faq.q: What are the must-try foods when visiting Chiang Rai?
faq.a: Northern Thai food you can't miss in Chiang Rai: rice noodles with nam ngiao (try Pa Suk Nam Ngiao), khao soi (Khao Soi Islam Chiang Rai), sai ua, khua laab, gaeng hang le, and khao kan jin. For desserts, Choui Fong's green tea cake and the homemade baked goods at riverside cafés like Chivit Thamma Da and Melt in Your Mouth.

faq.q: How much does food in Chiang Rai cost?
faq.a: À la carte and noodle restaurants like nam ngiao or khao soi start at around 40–60 THB per bowl. Northern Thai sit-down dishes are roughly 100–250 THB per dish. Cafés like Chivit Thamma Da or Melt in Your Mouth run around 250–500 THB per person including food and desserts. Choui Fong Tea Cafe is around 101–250 THB per person.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead?
faq.a: Street food and midday shops like Pa Suk Nam Ngiao or Khao Soi Islam are walk-in — no booking needed, but arrive early during peak hours. Kantoke restaurants with performances like Toke-Tong and Salungkham, and popular cafés on weekends, are worth calling ahead or arriving early to get a good table.

faq.q: Which restaurants are open in the evening or at night?
faq.a: For evening dining, Toke-Tong is open late with traditional performance. Paam Sai Ua and Salungkham are both open through the evening. Hlu Lam Rob Wiang and Laab Sanam Kila work well for early-evening meals. Nam ngiao and khao soi restaurants are mainly late-morning to afternoon — plan those for daytime.
